RESTORATION
CARBON
CARDIGAN BAY
· EDITED BY E.MOREL
Three years on, the Cardigan Bay saltmarsh is holding sediment faster than projected.

When we first underwrote the Cardigan rewetting in 2021, the modelled accretion curve was generous — 4.1 mm/yr against a 3.2 mm baseline. The basin has now logged 11.2 mm in the most recent monitoring window, an unhurried but unmistakable departure. We spent eight days walking transects with the Powys stewards and reading the sediment traps. What we found was not a miracle, only a slow refusal to stop working.

The Foundry's continued commitment to this place is a matter of patience capital — a fund that does not flinch when the line on the chart goes briefly the wrong way. Read on for the full ledger entry, hectare-by-hectare uptake, and the partner brief from Carreg-y-Llan.

SLOW REWILDING
Beaver dam analogues at Glen Lomas: first measurable channel widening.

Twelve months after the first BDA cluster went in, we walked the burn with the steward and a quiet hydrologist. The channel has widened by 2.4 metres at the deepest pool, and the side-banks are softening. There is also, against everyone's expectations, an otter.

From the Carpathian Trust: thirty hectares of old-growth beech now under perpetual protection.

Our partner trust in Brașov has closed the long-pending easement on the Bucegi escarpment block. We co-underwrote the title work and the first three years of warden salaries. A short summary of the legal envelope, the warden plan, and the new boundary survey.

Year-three serviceá audit, Loiá dam planting: 78.4% across 142,000 stems.

The Loiá audit returned cleanly. Of the 142,000 stems planted across the four sub-parcels in winter 2021, 78.4% are alive and recognisable. Cork-oak takes the prize; carob is sulking. The full audit table, with mortality clustering and replanting plan for autumn.
